surfaces.part: top cap band of the machine body
front face: display slot, ticket button grid, dispenser tray

answer.evidence: The red body has a band at rows 1-6 (row 0 is the narrower outline). Row 6 is a lighter front-edge line (L=128 against L=107 above), and row 7 is a dark eave shadow (L=62). Below that, rows 8-31 form a vertical front face with a display slot, a button grid and a dispenser tray. The face is 24 rows tall and has no side face. The top band has an edge line and shadow, so it counts as a top surface and not a plain front-facing cornice.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small upright red vending machine, a standing prop like the references. The measured facts are strong: 27 visible tones per 16x16 tile against 17-20 for the stall and well, 0% near-flat coverage, and only 6% neutral dark edge pixels. The outline is therefore tinted, a dark red-brown beside the red body, and not a neutral black line. By eye the body has several red steps, a lit panel, a button grid and a dispensing slot, so there are no large flat fills. The pixel art is small and a little less textured than the stall or well, but it is not thinner or more sticker-like than the references.

The outline reads as a dark red-brown that leans toward the body colour, not a neutral black line. Only 6% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 33% for the roofed well and 100% for the lamp. It has 27 visible tones per 16x16 tile, above the stall (17), well (20) and hedge (9).
